label: miso 88 egrid hr
definition: miso-88: the 2026-07-24-miso-86-netrev-margin keeper replayed byte-faithfully with a SINGLE delta that is a data correction, not a flag — the eGRID plant-heat-rate boundary reconciliation. Riverside Energy Center (55641) carried 14.964 MMBtu/MWh because eGRID divided the whole CEMS facility's heat input (which also covers co-located West Riverside, EIA 64020) by only the Riverside plant's net generation; reconciled from eGRID's own unit rows to 6.880. Zero degrees of freedom, verified blast radius 3 rows / 1 plant / MISO only. Closes the keeper's sole load-bearing volume fail: C1 fuel-mix FAIL → PASS in all three years. Closed the keeper's last load-bearing FAIL to a single criterion; RE-GATED 2026-07-26 (miso-90, owner decision) to a caveated pass when C3b-2025 (NRMSE 0.208) was ledgered as an instrument-blocked measurement gap — a ~10 GW under-derate of 2025 summer-peak fossil availability whose only record is published at a fuel-blind grain, with every enumerated instrument refuted, data-blocked or measured inert (miso-89). Ledgered caveats 3/3 (C3a, C3b, C3c). DETERMINATION RESTATED 2026-07-27 to NOT-YET (miso-96, owner decision): rubric v2.8 (commit ab7ce17, the ERCOT-121 coal gate-blindness correction) added the merchant COAL classes to the C7 gate set, exposing a REAL and previously-INVISIBLE diurnal-shape failure this keeper had carried in all three years -- D-1 COAL_PRB off-peak cv_ratio 0.453/0.441/0.364 against a >=0.50 gate. C7 is protective and hard, so it forces NOT-YET and cannot be ledgered (the ledgered budget is 3/3 saturated regardless). The scorer got sharper; the keeper did not get worse, and nothing about the run, its bundle or its config changed -- this is a scoring restatement only, per rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] (the honest gate made the verdict worse, so it is root-caused rather than buried). Root cause is ATTRIBUTED and proven by A/B: the miso-66 committed-band take-or-pay discount prices an accounting-period tonnage obligation (a sunk FIXED cost) as an unconditional per-hour MARGINAL subsidy, pinning 9,403 MW of regulated PRB inframarginal in all 8760 h. The candidate fix (arm 2026-07-27-miso-96-sunkfixed-takeorpay) clears 2023/2024 shape but breaks C1 fuel-mix and C5a CO2 and was REJECTED, so the keeper designation is unchanged. Evidence: results/calibration/FINDING-miso96-coal-prb-offpeak-2026-07.md; open lane: a minimum-take constraint priced by its own dual.
market_story: This is a measurement fix, not a market lever — and it shows how a single bad input can masquerade as a market-structure problem. A 675 MW combined cycle was carrying a heat rate of 14.96 MMBtu/MWh, roughly twice what any combined cycle can physically achieve, because eGRID keys its plant sheet on ORISPL while CEMS reports co-located plants under one facilityId: Riverside Energy Center and the newer West Riverside block 454 m away share CEMS facility 55641, so eGRID's heat-rate numerator spanned both blocks while its denominator counted only one. The consequence in the market was concrete — at ~$3/MMBtu gas the plant offered near $45/MWh against ~$20/MWh for comparable MISO CCs, which is above most of the MISO coal fleet, so the LP simply never committed it: model capacity factor 0.01 against an actual 0.60. That one plant was most of the CC_REGULAR volume miss the previous two keepers had been chasing through offer bands, tranche splits and availability, none of which were the cause. Restoring the measured 6.88 puts 535 MW back into the merit order below coal and closes C1 in all three years. It also pushes prices slightly DOWN, which widens the two price crossings — that was pre-registered in the charter before the solve, and the accurate input stays in regardless (rules 1/11): the residual is now a price-formation question about 2025 summer body hours, not a volume question, and it is a cleaner question than the one it replaced.
